## Trial `mariadb-galera-cold-restart-ubun__KH6aumt`

**Verifier decision: Not Successfully Evaluated.** The executor eventually stood up a functioning three-member MariaDB Galera cluster on node1-3 after discovering that the Ubuntu 16.04 apt-repo mariadb-server-10.0/galera-3 combination lacked a working WSREP-enabled mysqld, and instead deployed a MariaDB 10.1.48 i686 binary tarball with a custom systemd unit, datadir, and config. Final checks confirm cluster_size=3, all three synced, and application data (appdb.orders) present and queryable. However, the trace never demonstrates the specific contract requirement of bringing the entire cluster down together for a maintenance window and restoring it with prior committed writes intact — the only simultaneous three-node stop happened against the pre-Galera, broken install, and later restart testing was limited to rolling single-node stop/start cycles, with the sample data insert as the final command and no subsequent restart to confirm persistence. The build-out also left several uncleaned troubleshooting artifacts (added amd64 multiarch, a 3GB swapfile, a large build toolchain, and multi-hundred-MB leftover tarballs) that were not needed by the final solution.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Deploy a three-member MariaDB Galera cluster across node1, node2, and node3 holding application data.
  - **Why:** After extensive troubleshooting (the Ubuntu-repo mariadb-server-10.0/galera-3 combo lacked working WSREP support in the shipped mysqld binary), the executor built a working stack from the MariaDB 10.1.48 i686 binary tarball with the apt galera-3 provider library, installed it identically on all three nodes, and bootstrapped/joined them. Final status checks on node1 after all three nodes were online show wsrep_cluster_size=3, wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced, and wsrep_incoming_addresses listing all three node IPs. An appdb.orders table with three rows was created and confirmed via SELECT on node1 while the cluster reported all three members synced.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e16d6317e664458f`, `cmd-3539fe7a19d44ada`, `cmd-8c5bdc31d5dd430c`, `cmd-7e04e4c511a24738`
- **req-2 — Partially satisfied:** Bring the cluster down completely for a maintenance window and bring it back afterward with every committed write still present and all three members serving again.
  - **Why:** The only full three-node simultaneous stop observed in the trace (cmd-f9f5ae7953a14963, cmd-eab0f1bb9d5d46d2, cmd-3881fd31d32d46d7) occurred against the original, non-wsrep-capable mariadb-server-10.0 install before the working Galera stack existed, so it does not demonstrate the required maintenance-window transition for the final system. On the working 10.1.48 stack, the executor only performed sequential single-node stop/start cycles (node2 stop+restart, then node1 mysqladmin shutdown+systemctl restart) while the other two nodes stayed up, each time rejoining via SST/IST back to cluster_size=3. No evidence shows all three Galera nodes stopped together and cold-started together, and the only application data insert occurred as the final command in the trace with no subsequent restart to confirm the write survived a restart cycle.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-f9f5ae7953a14963`, `cmd-eab0f1bb9d5d46d2`, `cmd-3881fd31d32d46d7`, `cmd-e91f35db555f422e`, `cmd-6446f1119f5e44ce`, `cmd-9ef0ef557a734da6`, `cmd-8b30c853b2a54e45`, `cmd-3539fe7a19d44ada`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.500**. Several state-changing detours were left unreverted after the executor pivoted away from them: `dpkg --add-architecture amd64` was enabled on node1 (cmd-b66b2433a6fa4fb7) to chase an amd64 package path that was ultimately abandoned in favor of a precompiled i686 tarball, and was never disabled; a 3GB swapfile was created on node1 (cmd-7e981cef545e41a5) and never removed; a full build toolchain (build-essential, cmake, bison, libssl-dev, etc., cmd-f2a3fec905c14421) was installed to attempt a from-source WSREP build that was abandoned once no wsrep code was found in the 10.0.38 source tree, and these packages were left installed; large downloaded artifacts (~280-395MB mariadb-10.1.48-linux-i686.tar.gz tarballs) were left in /tmp/src on all three nodes instead of being cleaned up once /opt/mariadb101 was populated. On the positive side, the executor did clean up several dead-end artifacts: the amd64 dpkg -x extraction at /opt/mdb64 (cmd-8c8f2138212440c5), the earlier failed /opt/mariadb 10.0.38 build directory (cmd-3dda4aed878f4a8f), and stale source directories/tarballs. The purge of the original broken mariadb-server-10.0/galera-3 packages and datadir (cmd-62c60c55c5ea45a8 and peers) was a necessary corrective step, not unwanted residue. None of the leftovers are destructive or security-weakening, but they represent real, uncleaned disk/package residue from troubleshooting paths that did not contribute to the final solution.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-b66b2433a6fa4fb7`, `cmd-7e981cef545e41a5`, `cmd-f2a3fec905c14421`, `cmd-84666e583ccf4ff1`, `cmd-e7d7c44fb8a94872`, `cmd-8c8f2138212440c5`, `cmd-3dda4aed878f4a8f`, `cmd-62c60c55c5ea45a8`
